newsitem.title: PERU: Detonations heard at site of Peru hostage crisis.
newsitem.headline: Detonations heard at site of Peru hostage crisis.

text.p: Several detonations, apparently gunfire, were heard early on Friday from inside the compound of the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, where Marxist rebels held 74 hostages, police said.
"It sounded like four gunshots from an AKM (automatic) rifle," a police officer on duty about a block from the site told Reuters.

The detonations -- heard at about 2:50 a.m. local time (0750 GMT) -- were followed by silence. No movement was seen inside the compound, which was stormed by about 20 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels Dec. 17.

Juan Carlos Mejia, head of Peru's crack SUAT police, said two MRTA rebels had been spotted in the rear of the compound before the detonations were heard, the local Panamericana television network reported.
Mejia told the network the men fired shots into the air, ran back toward the ambassador's home and fired two more shots.
Witnesses said police on patrol around the diplomatic mansion went to a high state of alert following the detonations.
Two policemen could be seen lying face down behind a tree, their rifles pointed toward the residence, about 300 feet (100 meters) from the compound's main entrance.
It was the second time this week that detonations have been heard at the hostage siege site in the middle of the night.
Two shots were heard early on Tuesday as a man, presumed to be one of the MRTA rebels, ran across the front part of the compound toward the building.
Several shots and explosions have been heard during the siege, now into its fourth week. On each occasion they have caused alarm but no injuries.
